name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita

criteria.description: Presence of tense blisters and erosions on trauma-prone skin areas
Linear deposition of IgG and/or C3 along the dermal-epidermal junction on direct immunofluorescence
Circulating autoantibodies against type VII collagen detected by ELISA or immunoblot
Subepidermal blister with minimal inflammatory infiltrate on skin biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical blistering, immunofluorescence findings, and serologic detection of anti-type VII collagen antibodies) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tense subepidermal blisters on trauma-prone skin
Skin fragility with scarring and milia formation

common.symptomName: Erosions and ulcerations following blister rupture

occasional.symptomName: Dyspareunia due to genital mucosal involvement

laboratory: Detection of circulating IgG autoantibodies against type VII collagen by ELISA
Direct immunofluorescence showing linear IgG and/or C3 deposits at the dermal-epidermal junction
imaging: Endoscopy may reveal esophageal strictures in mucosal involvement
genetic: No known inherited genetic mutations; disease is autoimmune and acquired
other: Response to immunosuppressive therapy supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Autoantibodies target BP180 and BP230, not type VII collagen
Photosensitivity with blistering on sun-exposed areas
Elevated porphyrin levels in urine and plasma
No autoantibodies against type VII collagen

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin blistering with extensive erosions
Mucosal involvement causing dysphagia or airway compromise
Signs of secondary infection or sepsis
references: Schmidt E, Zillikens D. Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita. Clin Dermatol. 2012;30(1):70-77.
Liu Z, Diaz LA. Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita: clinical presentation, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment. Clin Dermatol. 2012;30(1):14-25.
